# Independent native rotation fixtures

Original synthetic pixels, oracle adapter and drivers are CC0-1.0. The application executable is not included. `original-vectors.json` retains the 36 two-method cases generated earlier by an independently compiled public-API adapter. `extended-vectors.json` adds 266 deterministic cases generated by this directory's `oracle.cpp` and `generate.mjs`; expected values come from native library output, not the JavaScript port.

The library comes from the official Aseprite v1.3.18.5 source release:
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/releases/download/v1.3.18.5/Aseprite-v1.3.18.5-Source.zip

Its document library is separately MIT licensed:
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/v1.3.18.5/src/doc/README.md
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/v1.3.18.5/src/doc/LICENSE.txt

The production JavaScript is an attributed adaptation of those MIT algorithms. The earlier fixtures were generated before inspecting their implementation; the later independent adapter calls the original compiled library, including its fixed-point implementation.

Compile the adapter against an existing local build. Example paths from the verification environment:

```sh
clang++ -std=c++17 -O2 -DNDEBUG \
  -I/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/source/src \
  -I/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/source/laf \
  -I/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/build/laf \
  -I/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/build \
  -I/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/source/third_party \
  tests/fixtures/rotation-native/oracle.cpp \
  -L/tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/build/lib \
  -ldoc-lib -llaf-gfx -llaf-base -lfixmath-lib -lfmt -lobs -lcityhash -lz \
  /tmp/pixelwall-aseprite-oracle/skia/out/Release-arm64/libskia.a \
  -framework CoreFoundation -o /tmp/pixelwall-rotation-oracle
ROTATION_ORACLE=/tmp/pixelwall-rotation-oracle node tests/fixtures/rotation-native/generate.mjs
```

Protocol: method (0 Fast / 1 RotSprite), native pixel format (0 RGBA / 1 grayscale / 2 indexed / 3 bitmap), source width/height, destination width/height, transparent mask color, mask-present 0/1, eight integer corner coordinates, packed pixels, and optional binary source mask. The source and destination use the supplied mask color; RGBA/gray fixtures use zero alpha. Each output line has destination row-major packed pixels.

These tests pin integer-corner library behavior. They do not establish Aseprite UI angle-to-corner rounding. Source figures are original numerical patterns, not vendor artwork.
